newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times business - Nov 5.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times business - Nov 5.

text.p: The New York Times reported the following business stories on Tuesday:
- Carl Icahn submitted a list of 10 people whom he hopes will replace the current board of directors at RJR Nabisco Holdings Corp.
- U.S. federal investigators issued subpoenas seeking evidence to show that Texaco Inc executives destroyed documents sought in a discrimination lawsuit against the company.
- British Telecommunications Plc and MCI Communications Corp first considered other companies as potential partners before agreeing to merge with each other.
- British investment manager Invesco Plc agreed to buy AIM Management Group Inc for $1.6 billion.
- Conflicting reports about discussions between Norfolk Southern Corp and CSX Corp over the fate of Conrail Inc sent Conrail's stock lower.
- Sierra Health Services Inc saw its stock price fall after announcing that it had agreed to buy Physician Corp of America for $509.4 million.
- Prices of Treasury securities made modest gains in thin trading.
- Advertising agency A.W. Ayer & Partners won assignments from U S West Inc with about $60 million in billings.
- Oracle Corp said Thomson Consumer Electronics and Funai Electric Co would make set-top devices that link televisions to the Internet using its technology.
- Former vice president of operations at IBM Corp's Argentina operations insists he is a scapegoat in a corruption scandal.
- The shooting of U.S. entrepreneur Paul Tatum in Russia shows how foreigners can easily fall into bloody business disputes in the country's capital.
